items.title: Preflight: Agentic Last-Mile Verification for AI Software Supply Chains
items.summary: Software dependencies execute within the trust boundary of downstream applications, yet provenance, static analysis, and package-level behavioral approaches do not directly determine how a released artifact behaves for a specific program. We present Preflight, a program-scoped pre-execution verifier for Python dependencies that extracts application-referenced symbols, iteratively synthesizes and validates function-level harnesses, executes resolved artifacts in a restricted environment, records behavioral fingerprints, and compares target behavior against prior versions when suitable baselines exist. We evaluate Preflight on four real software-supply-chain incidents under five application contexts, a 100-package benign corpus, and a controlled function-level versus import-only ablation. Preflight returns malicious verdicts in four incident contexts and a clean verdict in the LiteLLM client context, where the affected proxy-server path is not exercised. All 100 evaluated benign packages receive clean verdicts, with zero observed false positives. In a controlled ablation on Ultralytics and ctx, function-level harnesses expose malicious behavior in both incidents, whereas import-only probing exposes neither. Together, these results show that conditioning behavioral verification on the downstream program can expose security-relevant dependency behavior while remaining selective on benign workloads.

items.title: Agentic Discovery of Simple Symbolic Inventory Policies
items.summary: Designing simple inventory policies becomes increasingly difficult as operational features and system configurations expand. We develop an Agentic Inventory-Policy Discovery System based on explicitly defined simple operational formula (SOF) policy and template classes. Large language models (LLMs) revise symbolic structures, while a numerical engine fits parameters separately for each instance and evaluates the induced policies. Multicriteria parent selection, state-specific operational diagnostics, and reusable symbolic motifs guide structural evolution. A three-stage progression develops shared templates across instances and configurations with varying state dimensions. Experiments on 15,600 instances spanning 50 demand distributions cover lead times, perishability, their combination, and lead times with limited customer patience. The discovered templates improve aggregate empirical performance over evaluated SOF benchmarks and are competitive with policies requiring more elaborate online computations. For a lost-sales system with a three-period lead time, we develop an average-cost decomposition and prove that, under specified demand and cost conditions, a capped dual-shortfall specialization of a discovered policy strictly outperforms every policy in the considered capped base-stock benchmark class. This analysis links the performance advantage to the discovered replenishment mechanism. Together, these results highlight the potential of agentic discovery to generate…

items.title: Multi-location Newsvendor: An Interpretable Inventory Policy
items.summary: We study a multilocation newsvendor problem in which inventory is chosen before demand is observed and surplus stock can subsequently be transshipped to locations with shortages. The objective is to minimize expected holding, backlog, and transportation costs over a metric network. Under uniform transportation costs, the optimality conditions balance local and aggregate demand coverage and reduce to a scalar search under mild regularity conditions. We use this structure to develop an interpretable iterative heuristic for general metrics. The heuristic calibrates effective transportation costs from lateral shipments under independent stocking and uses them to construct location-dependent pooling weights. These weights have a direct operational interpretation through the cost of serving demand at other locations. Under the stated assumptions, the heuristic recovers the exact uniform-metric solution. Numerical experiments on structured and random networks show costs close to the sampled optimum on average and substantial savings relative to independent stocking.

items.title: Network-Aware Reserve Procurement via Decision-Dependent Adaptive Robust Optimization
items.summary: Network congestion can hinder reserve deliverability, motivating network-aware reserve procurement. Existing adaptive robust optimization approaches overlook the dependence of uncertainty sets on reserve demand curves and renewable curtailment, which is important in systems with high levels of variable renewable energy. We address this using decisiondependent box uncertainty sets, whose bounds depend on reserve demand curves and day-ahead curtailment of variable renewable energy. We reformulate the problem using a primitive uncertainty set and solve it via column-and-constraint generation. On a 29- bus Great Britain system, the proposed method is more costeffective than the inscribed boxes method because it accounts for the potential of reserve activation to both aggravate and relieve network congestion, whereas the inscribed boxes method only captures the former. Cost savings stem from differences in energy and reserve schedules, including the beneficial simultaneous activation of upward and downward reserves for real-time balancing in some scenarios.

The various stages of order fulfilment are modelled through a formal mathematical framework, by defining disruption indicators computed from both historical and real-time data drawn from heterogeneous sources, including traffic and weather conditions and supplier dispatch readiness. Building on a graph-based representation of the supply chain, stochastic methods based on Markov chains are applied to estimate delivery times, detect schedule deviations, quantify prediction uncertainty, and produce interpretable metrics to support operational decision-making. Within the M4ESTRO project, the proposed framework was applied to build a web application for real-time tracking of inbound logistics, and was validated in a use case with an industrial project partner.
